generation.explanation: In flat (Euclidean) geometry, draw a line through the triangle’s top vertex parallel to its base. The two base angles reappear beside the top angle because parallel lines have equal alternate interior angles. Together, those three angles form a straight angle—180°. Drag the top vertex to see that the individual angles change, but their sum does not.
